candidate.blueprint_topic: Preventive vaccination teaching for adults with chronic liver disease
candidate.educational_objective: Teach adults with chronic liver disease to receive indicated hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccination according to the current CDC adult immunization schedule rather than assuming vaccination is limited to occupational-risk groups or completed after one dose.

options.A: Review the current CDC vaccination recommendations with the client and arrange completion of indicated hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccine series because chronic liver disease is a specific indication/risk factor.
options.B: Vaccination is unnecessary because hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccines are recommended only for healthcare personnel with occupational exposure.
options.C: One dose of either vaccine guarantees complete lifelong protection, so there is no reason to complete the recommended series.
options.D: Chronic liver disease is a contraindication to hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccination because vaccination can worsen cirrhosis.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The current CDC adult immunization schedule identifies chronic liver disease as an indication for hepatitis A vaccination because these clients are at increased risk for severe outcomes from hepatitis A infection. For hepatitis B, adults age 60 years or older with risk factors for HBV infection—including chronic liver disease—should receive a HepB vaccine series. The current CDC adult schedule remains the July 2, 2025 schedule under the March 16, 2026 court order, with the schedule page explicitly identifying it as current in 2026. B is incorrect because hepatitis vaccination recommendations extend well beyond occupational risk. C is incorrect because the recommended vaccine course depends on product and requires completion of the indicated series; a single dose should not be presented as guaranteeing complete lifelong protection. D is incorrect because chronic liver disease is an indication/risk factor supporting vaccination, not a blanket contraindication. The final item uses an age and disease state that make both HepA and HepB recommendations directly supported by current CDC guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports HepA vaccination for adults with chronic liver disease and HepB vaccination for adults age 60 or older with chronic liver disease as an HBV risk factor; CDC explicitly identifies the July 2, 2025 adult schedule as the current schedule in 2026 under the March 16, 2026 court order.
